newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish museum shuts controversial bushman exhibit.
newsitem.headline: Spanish museum shuts controversial bushman exhibit.

text.p: Diplomatic skirmishing over the embalmed body of an African bushman on display since 1916 in the Spanish town of Banyoles, has forced the town to close the exhibit, officials said on Wednesday.
"It's been withdrawn from public display out of respect for the sensitivity of the black African countries," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
"It would have been convenient if the stuffed black man had never been exhibited, as this affair is not helping Spain's image among the African countries."

Objections to the exhibit started five years ago, just ahead of the 1992 Olympic Games in Barcelona, when a Haitian doctor protested that the display was racist and tried to get African countries to boycott the Games.
The doctor later filed a lawsuit against Banyoles over the exhibit.
Senegal Foreign Minister Moustapha Niasse recently branded the exhibit "inexcusable" and told his Spanish counterpart the case would be brought before the Organisation of African Unity.

Joan Solana, mayor of the Catalonian town, had long resisted pressure to close the exhibit but on Tuesday changed his mind, risking the wrath of his voters who treasure the display in their municipal natural history museum.
"I've decided to close the exhibition room in order to cool the polemic and avoid a diplomatic conflict for Spain," he said.
"It has done a lot of damage to this city, being accused of racism when there are 600 fully integrated African immigrants who live here and accept the exhibit as something natural."
The body of the bushman, which was dug up and embalmed in 1830 in what is now Botswana, is in an upright position, holding a spear and wearing a loincloth.
It is displayed in a glass case in a room containing other anthropological artefacts, including skulls, pieces of human skin, and embalmed embryos.

"This is all very absurd," museum curator Georgina Gratacos said. "Throughout European culture there are human remains that are exhibited in museums: Egyptian mummies, the iceman found recently and other examples."
